# Uploading Data file

```{r}
nhanes_newvars <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "nhanes_newvars_zscore.rds"))
```


# Part D

## Evalation of Cell Counts in Exposure `screen_quart`

```{r}

## Examination of Exposure & Evaluation of cell counts ##
# setting male analytic sample
subpop_male <- subset(nhanes_newvars, 
                 subpop1 ==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")

# setting female analytic sample
subpop_female <- subset(nhanes_newvars, subpop1 ==1 & RIAGENDR =="Female")

# examination of exposure (screen time) and EMM among males 
# frequency table of males
subpop_male %>% 
  mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) %>% 
  tabyl(screen_quart, fsdch_2cat)

# examination of exposure (screen time) and EMM among females
# frequency table of females
subpop_female |> 
  mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) |> 
  tabyl(screen_quart, fsdch_2cat)
```

## Evaluation of Outcome `z_haz_adj`

```{r}
## Examination of Outcome from Part C + Graphical Visualization ##

attach(nhanes_newvars)
## Primary survey design
nhanes_design_full <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTMEC6YR,
  nest = TRUE,
  data = nhanes_newvars)

# Isolating analytic subpop
subpop_design <- subset(nhanes_design_full, subpop1 == 1)

## Mean & Central Tendency 
#Estimate the mean and central tendency of BMD correcting for stratified sampling and survey weights. 
## correcting for stratified sampling and survey weights
svymean(~z_haz_adj, design = subpop_design)


#Estimating the mean and central tendency of BMD by screen time quartiles
svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subpop_design, 
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

#Estimating the mean and central tendency of BMD by screen time quartiles & SEX
svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"), # by sex male
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"), # by sex female
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

# weighted histogram of BMD adjusted z-score
## weighted histogram of analytic sample
svyhist(~z_haz_adj, 
        design = subpop_design, 
        breaks = 30)

# weighted histogram by male sex
svyhist(~z_haz_adj, 
        design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"), 
        breaks = 30)

# weighted histogram by female sex
svyhist(~z_haz_adj, 
        design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"), 
        breaks = 30)


# weighted boxplot of BMD adjusted z-score
## weighted boxplot
svyboxplot(z_haz_adj~1, 
           design = subpop_design)

# weighted boxplot by male sex
svyboxplot(z_haz_adj~1, 
           design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

# weighted boxplot by female sex
svyboxplot(z_haz_adj~1, 
           design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"))
```

## Visualization of Exposure & Outcome With Linearity & Normality

```{r}

## Visualization of Linearity in Exposure and Outcome ##
# Among male subpop
ggplot(subpop_male, 
       aes(x = as.numeric(screen_quart), y = z_haz_adj)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 1, alpha = .6, width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 8, shape = 18) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Screen time Quartiles", 
       y = "BMD adjusted z-scores",
       title = "BMD z-scores vs. screen time quartiles among 8-17 y.o males",
       caption = "Diamonds = screen time level averages") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 10, vjust = 1, hjust=1))

# Among female subpop
ggplot(subpop_female, 
       aes(x = as.numeric(screen_quart), y = z_haz_adj)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 1, alpha = .6, width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 8, shape = 18) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Screen time Quartiles", 
       y = "BMD adjusted z-scores",
       title = "BMD z-scores vs. screen time quartiles among 8-17 y.o females",
       caption = "Diamonds = screen time level averages") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 10, vjust = 1, hjust=1))

## Normality##
##Evaluation of distribution of outcome with QQ plot among male subpop
# linear regression
model_male <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart), 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

#augment to extract residuals (.resid)
aug_male <- augment(model_male)
glimpse(aug_male)

#creating QQ plot
ggplot(aug_male, 
       aes(sample = .resid)) + 
  stat_qq() + 
  stat_qq_line()

##Evaluation of distribution of outcome with QQ plot among female subpop
# linear regression
model_female <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart), 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"))

#augment to extract residuals (.resid)
aug_female <- augment(model_female)
glimpse(aug_female)

#creating QQ plot
ggplot(aug_female, 
       aes(sample = .resid)) + 
  stat_qq() + 
  stat_qq_line()
```

## Visualization of Linearity of Other Continuous Independent Variables

```{r}
## Age as a Continuous Variable ##
# creating a scatterplot in male subpop
nhanes_newvars%>% 
  filter(subpop1==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = RIDAGEYR, 
             y = z_haz_adj)) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height = 0.1)) + 
  labs(title = "Scatterplot of Age and BMD z-score", 
      y = "BMD z-score")

# overlaying a LOESS (locally weighted regression) plot
nhanes_newvars%>% 
  filter(subpop1==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = z_haz_adj, 
             y = RIDAGEYR)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", 
              span = 0.75, 
              se = F, 
              color = "green") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", 
              span = 0.25, 
              se = F, 
              color = "red", 
              linetype = 2) + 
  theme_classic() 

# Fit the crude model with the linear age term and output the linear predictor
## Using survey specifications coded above with same analytic sample
## run the model among males
crude_age_model <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~RIDAGEYR, 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_age_model)

# Get fitted values
aug_age <- augment(crude_age_model)

# plot the model-predicted linear outcome versus age
ggplot(data = aug_age, 
       aes(x = RIDAGEYR, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Age at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor") + 
  theme_classic()

## Higher order predictors
# find mean in subpop
svymean(~RIDAGEYR, design = subpop_design) # weighted mean = 12.482

# create centered variables
nhanes_newvars <- nhanes_newvars %>% 
  mutate(agec = RIDAGEYR - 12.482, 
         agec_sq = agec^2, 
         agec_cu = agec^3)

## Quadratic model
## re-run survey specifications
nhanes_design_quad <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTMEC6YR,
  nest = TRUE,
  data = nhanes_newvars)

# setting analytic sample
subpop_quad <- subset(nhanes_design_quad, 
                 subpop1 ==1)

## run the model
crude_model_quad <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~agec+agec_sq, 
                      design = subset(subpop_quad, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_model_quad)

# Get fitted values
model_aug_quad <- augment(crude_model_quad)

ggplot(data = model_aug_quad, 
       aes(x = agec + 12.482, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Age at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor", 
       title = "Quadratic Model") + 
  theme_classic()

## Cubic Model
## run the model
crude_model_cube <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~agec+agec_sq+agec_cu, 
                       design = subset(subpop_quad, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_model_cube)

# Get fitted values
model_aug_cube <- augment(crude_model_cube)

ggplot(data = model_aug_cube, 
       aes(x = agec + 12.482, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Age at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor", 
       title = "Cubic Model") + 
  theme_classic()

library(describedata)
gladder(subpop_male$RIDAGEYR) # looking to see if age should be transformed 
# to another power not evaluated. It looks like identity is appropriate.
```

## Estimates of Fully Adjusted Measure of Association

```{r}

# need to relevel the race/ethnicity variable
levels(nhanes_newvars$RIDRETH3)
class(nhanes_newvars$RIDRETH3)

nhanes_newvars <- nhanes_newvars |> 
  mutate(
    race_eth = fct_relevel(RIDRETH3, "Non-Hispanic White")
  )
  
# checking
levels(nhanes_newvars$race_eth)

## resetting the primary survey design 
nhanes_design_full <- svydesign(id = ~SDMVPSU, 
                                strata = ~SDMVSTRA, 
                                weights= ~WTMEC6YR, 
                                nest = TRUE, 
                                data = nhanes_newvars)

# Isolating analytic subpop

subpop_design <- subset(nhanes_design_full, subpop1 == 1)

## Fully adjusted model
# creating the full model 
full_adjust_model <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart) + RIDAGEYR + factor(parent_edu) + factor(race_eth) + INDFMPIR + BMXHT, 
                            design = subpop_design)


summary(full_adjust_model)

# creating the full model among males
full_male_model <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart) + RIDAGEYR + factor(parent_edu) + factor(race_eth) + INDFMPIR + BMXHT, 
                            design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(full_male_model)

# creating the full model among females
full_female_model <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart) + RIDAGEYR + factor(parent_edu) + factor(race_eth) + INDFMPIR + BMXHT, 
                            design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"))

summary(full_female_model)

```

# Table 2 + 3 Creation

## Table 2 Males

```{r}
library(srvyr)
# 1. Distribution of Screen Quartile (Unweighted N, Weighted %)
w_pct <- tbl_svysummary(
  data = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR == "Male"), 
  include = screen_quart, 
  missing = "no", 
  statistic = list(all_categorical() ~ "{n_unweighted} ({p}%)"), 
  label = list(screen_quart = "Screen Quartile")
)

male_design <- subset(nhanes_design_full, subpop1 == 1 & RIAGENDR == "Male")


# 2. Mean BMD Table (Vertical Layout)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate weighted means and SEs by screen_quart
bmd_by_q <- svyby(~z_haz_adj, ~screen_quart, male_design, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a named lookup vector formatted as "Mean (SE)"
bmd_lookup <- setNames(
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", bmd_by_q$z_haz_adj, bmd_by_q$se),
  as.character(bmd_by_q$screen_quart)
)

# Copy w_pct structure and map the Mean (SE) values onto the quartile levels
m_mean <- w_pct
m_mean$table_body$stat_0 <- ifelse(
  m_mean$table_body$row_type == "level",
  bmd_lookup[as.character(m_mean$table_body$label)],
  NA_character_
)

# 3. Unadjusted Regression Table
t2 <- tbl_regression(
  model_male, 
  include = "factor(screen_quart)",
  label = list("factor(screen_quart)" = "Screen Quartile"), 
  exponentiate = FALSE, 
  conf.level = 0.95, 
  conf.int = TRUE
) 

# 4. Adjusted Regression Table
t3 <- tbl_regression(
  full_male_model, 
  exponentiate = FALSE, 
  include = "factor(screen_quart)", 
  label = list("factor(screen_quart)" = "Screen Quartile"), 
  conf.level = 0.95, 
  conf.int = TRUE
)

# Harmonize internal variable names to match w_pct ("screen_quart")
t2$table_body$variable[t2$table_body$variable == "factor(screen_quart)"] <- "screen_quart"
t3$table_body$variable[t3$table_body$variable == "factor(screen_quart)"] <- "screen_quart"

merged_male_table <- tbl_merge(
  tbls = list(w_pct, m_mean, t2, t3),
  tab_spanner = c(
    "**Sample Size**",
    "**Mean BMD (SE)**",
    "**Unadjusted Model**",
    "**Adjusted Model** <sup>2</sup>"
  )
) %>%
  modify_caption(
    caption = "Table 2. Associations beetween daily average screen time and TBLH BMD z-scores scores in unadjusted and fully adjusted linear regression models among male children aged 8- 17 y.o (n = 2,044)"
  ) %>%
  modify_header(
    all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**<br>N = {n_unweighted}"
  ) %>%
  as_gt() %>%
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = "² Fully adjusted models were adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, height (in cm), household reference person's education level, and household income evaluated at the federal poverty level."
  )

merged_male_table


# attempting to save the table 
gt::gtsave(merged_male_table, filename = "Table2_Males_zscore.png") #save male as png


```

## Table 3 Females

```{r}

)
  
# 3. Unadjusted Regression Table

    "**Unadjusted Model**",
    "**Adjusted Model** <sup>2</sup>"
  )
) %>%
  modify_caption(caption = "Table 3. Associations beetween daily average screen time and TBLH BMD raw scores in unadjusted and fully adjusted linear regression models among female children aged 8- 17 y.o (n = 1,953)") %>%
  modify_header(
    all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**<br>N = {n_unweighted}"

merged_female_table
```

## Evaluation of Effect Measure Modification Food Security- Interaction

```{r}
## Evaluating EMM with interaction term in the model
# Among Males
int_male_model <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart)*factor(fsdch_2cat) + RIDAGEYR + factor(parent_edu) + factor(race_eth) + INDFMPIR + BMXHT, 
                            design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

# view the model
summ(int_male_model, 
     confint = T, 
     ci.width = 0.95, 
     exp = F)

# omnibus nested F-test
anova(full_male_model, int_male_model, method = "Wald", test = "F")


# Among Females
int_female_model <- svyglm(z_haz_adj~factor(screen_quart)*factor(fsdch_2cat) + RIDAGEYR + factor(parent_edu) + factor(race_eth) + INDFMPIR + BMXHT, 
                            design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"))

# view the model
summ(int_female_model, 
     confint = T, 
     ci.width = 0.95, 
     exp = F)

# omnibus nested F-test
anova(full_female_model, int_female_model, method = "Wald", test = "F")

```

```{r}
#Estimating the mean and central tendency of BMD by screen time quartiles and EMM's
## Among Males
svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male" & fsdch_2cat == "High/Marginal Food Security"), # by sex male & FS
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male" & fsdch_2cat == "Low/Very Low Food Security"), # by sex male & FINS
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)


## Among Females
svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female" & fsdch_2cat == "High/Marginal Food Security"),# by sex female & FS
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

svyby(formula = ~z_haz_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female" & fsdch_2cat == "Low/Very Low Food Security"),# by sex female & FINS
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)
```

## Table 4 + 5 Creation

### Table 4 Males

```{r}
# 1. Distribution of Screen Quartile (Unweighted N, Weighted %)
fs_w_pct <- tbl_svysummary(
  data = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR == "Male" & fsdch_2cat=="High/Marginal Food Security"), 
  include = screen_quart, 
  missing = "no", 
  statistic = list(all_categorical() ~ "{n_unweighted} ({p}%)"), 
  label = list(screen_quart = "Screen Quartile")
) |> modify_header(stat_0 ~ "")


# 2. Mean BMD Table (Vertical Layout)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate weighted means and SEs by screen_quart
bmd_by_q <- svyby(~z_haz_adj, ~screen_quart, subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR == "Male" & fsdch_2cat=="High/Marginal Food Security"), svymean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a named lookup vector formatted as "Mean (SE)"
bmd_lookup <- setNames(
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", bmd_by_q$z_haz_adj, bmd_by_q$se),
  as.character(bmd_by_q$screen_quart)
)

# Copy w_pct structure and map the Mean (SE) values onto the quartile levels
fs_mean <- fs_w_pct
fs_mean$table_body$stat_0 <- ifelse(
  fs_mean$table_body$row_type == "level",
  bmd_lookup[as.character(fs_mean$table_body$label)],
  NA_character_
)

fs_mean <- fs_mean |> 
  modify_header(stat_0 ~ "")


fs_mean

# 4. Adjusted Regression Table
t4 <- tbl_regression(
  reg_male_fs, 
  include = "factor(screen_quart)", 
  label = list("factor(screen_quart)" = "Screen Quartile"), 
  conf.level = 0.95, 
  conf.int = TRUE
)

# Harmonize internal variable names to match w_pct ("screen_quart")
t4$table_body$variable[t4$table_body$variable == "factor(screen_quart)"] <- "screen_quart"

strat_male_fs <- tbl_merge(
  tbls = list(fs_w_pct, fs_mean, t4),
  tab_spanner = c(
    "**Sample Size**",
    "**Mean BMD z-score (SE)**",
    "**Stratified Model** <sup>3</sup>"
  )
) %>%
  modify_caption(
    caption = "Table 4. Associations beetween daily average screen time and TBLH BMD raw scores among male children aged 8- 17 y.o stratified by food security status (n = 2,044)"
  )

strat_male_fs


# 1. Distribution of Screen Quartile (Unweighted N, Weighted %)

  data = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR == "Male" & fsdch_2cat=="Low/Very Low Food Security"),

)

# 2. Mean BMD Table (Vertical Layout)

bmd_by_q <- svyby(~z_haz_adj, ~screen_quart, subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR == "Male" & fsdch_2cat=="Low/Very Low Food Security"), svymean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a named lookup vector formatted as "Mean (SE)"
bmd_lookup <- setNames(
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", bmd_by_q$z_haz_adj, bmd_by_q$se),
  as.character(bmd_by_q$screen_quart)
)

# Copy w_pct structure and map the Mean (SE) values onto the quartile levels

fins_mean$table_body$stat_0 <- ifelse(

  bmd_lookup[as.character(fins_mean$table_body$label)],
  NA_character_

fins_mean

# 4. Adjusted Regression Table
t5 <- tbl_regression(
  reg_male_fins, 
  exponentiate = FALSE, 
  include = "factor(screen_quart)", 
  label = list("factor(screen_quart)" = "Screen Quartile"), 
  conf.level = 0.95, 
  conf.int = TRUE
)

  tab_spanner = c(

    "**Stratified Model** <sup>3</sup>"
  )
) 


strat_male_fins


# Stack them vertically
stacked_male_table <- tbl_stack(
  tbls = list(strat_male_fs, strat_male_fins),
  group_header = c("Food Secure Males", "Food Insecure Males") # Creates section headers
) %>%
  modify_caption(
    caption = "Table 4. Associations beetween daily average screen time and TBLH BMD raw scores among male children aged 8- 17 y.o<br>stratified by food security status² (n = 2,044)"
  ) %>% 
  as_gt() %>%
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = "² P-value for omnibus nested F-test (0.42)"
  ) |> 
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = "³ Fully adjusted models were adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, height (in cm), household reference person's education level, and household income evaluated at the federal poverty level."
  )

stacked_male_table


# attempting to save the table 
gt::gtsave(stacked_male_table, filename = "Table4_Males_zscore.png") #save male as png
```
